s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic musculoskeletal pain and stress fractures with abnormal bone mineralization
salient_findings: Stress fractures of the left rib, left sacrum, and left femoral neck
Abnormal bone densitometry with Z-scores of −2.5 in the lumbar spine and −1.9 in the femoral neck
key_facts: 2-year history of hip pain following low-impact falls
Elevated alkaline phosphatase level of 220 U/L
Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) level of 1241 RU/mL
Bone densitometry showed Z-scores of −2.5 in the lumbar spine and −1.9 in the femoral neck
Genetic evaluation for hypophosphatemic disorders was unremarkable
Family history was negative for bone disease

raw.rationale: Elevated FGF23 level and presence of an intracortical lesion with high SUV on gallium-68 DOTATATE PET/MRI suggest a tumor-related cause of hypophosphatemia
raw.anchor_refutation: Genetic evaluation for X-linked hypophosphatemia was unremarkable and family history was negative for bone disease, making X-linked hypophosphatemia less likely

rejected.label: X-linked hypophosphatemia
rejected.why: Genetic evaluation was unremarkable and family history was negative

rejected.label: Hypophosphatemic rickets
rejected.why: Patient's age and presentation do not align with typical rickets diagnosis

rejected.label: Osteomalacia
rejected.why: While patient has low phosphorus and elevated alkaline phosphatase, the presence of a tumor suggests a more specific diagnosis

rejected.label: Fibroblast growth factor 23-related hypophosphatemia
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes tumor-induced osteomalacia, but the specific diagnosis of tumor-induced osteomalacia is more precise
